question: A patient with severe liver disease looks restless, seems confused, and has a fast heart rate with dropping blood pressure. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a comprehensive assessment for internal bleeding and report changes immediately
options.B: Document the findings in the chart and schedule a routine check for the next morning
options.C: Apply warm compresses to the patient's limbs to improve peripheral circulation
options.D: Encourage the patient to get out of bed and walk around the ward to ease restlessness

explanation: Restlessness, confusion, and dropping vitals are classic red flags! They can mean internal bleeding is happening, which needs urgent action.

question: Which color of waste bag is standard for infectious clinical waste and pathological specimens?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Blue
options.C: Clear
options.D: Black

explanation: Yellow bags and bins are globally recognized for infectious and pathological waste that requires incineration. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h3)

question: Which type of stretcher splits into two halves so you can slide it under a patient without rolling them?

options.A: Scoop stretcher
options.B: Basket stretcher
options.C: Canvas folding stretcher
options.D: Rigid spine board

explanation: Spot on! A scoop stretcher splits lengthwise, making it super helpful when you want to avoid rolling a fragile patient.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop in the human body?

options.A: Parathyroid hormone halting when blood calcium levels normalize
options.B: Insulin stopping the release of glucose once blood sugar drops
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH release when levels are high

explanation: Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback amplifies a signal! During labor, oxytocin makes contractions stronger, which releases even *more* oxytocin until the baby is born.

question: What do we call the signs of pregnancy that are felt and reported only by the mother herself?

options.A: Diagnostic signs
options.B: Presumptive signs
options.C: Probable signs
options.D: Positive signs

explanation: You've got this! Presumptive signs are subjective changes the mother experiences firsthand, like missed periods or sore breasts. Think of them as clues she notices herself.

question: What is the difference between client privacy and client confidentiality?

options.A: Privacy refers to hospital finances, whereas confidentiality refers to drug stock inventories
options.B: Privacy is a legal rule, whereas confidentiality is merely a personal suggestion
options.C: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies exclusively to nursing assistants
options.D: Privacy involves the client's body and physical space, whereas confidentiality involves keeping health information secret

explanation: Privacy protects physical boundaries, while confidentiality protects verbal and written medical data shared in professional trust. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: What is the main job of the methodology section in a research proposal?

options.A: To list every book ever written on nursing
options.B: To praise previous researchers in the field
options.C: To prove that the researcher has a large budget
options.D: To explain how the study will be carried out

explanation: The methodology is your step-by-step game plan. It explains the exact tools, steps, and designs you will use to gather and check your data.

question: What causes the nutritional paradox where a person is both overweight and undernourished?

options.A: Eating many cheap calories that lack essential micronutrients
options.B: Absorbing too many vitamins from cheap processed snacks
options.C: Consuming too much pure water alongside sugary drinks
options.D: Exercising too much while eating high-protein diets

explanation: When people fill up on cheap, heavy foods, they get plenty of energy (calories) but miss out on crucial vitamins and minerals. Great job thinking this through!

question: What does disease 'eradication' mean in public health?

options.A: Lowering local cases to an acceptable level
options.B: Eliminating a disease from one specific country
options.C: Permanent reduction to zero of worldwide incidence
options.D: Stopping an outbreak in a single hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! Eradication means the disease is completely wiped out across the entire globe, so we never have to fight it again. Smallpox is a great example!

question: What happens to the body during a state of positive energy balance?

options.A: It maintains a completely stable body weight
options.B: It burns stored fat to make up for a calorie deficit
options.C: It stores extra calories and gains weight
options.D: It stops all metabolic processes to save energy

explanation: When you take in more calories than you burn, the extra energy gets stored, primarily as fat, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h6)

question: A community has a very high percentage of children under the age of five. What service should the nurse prioritize based on this demographic?

options.A: Chronic disease management for the elderly
options.B: Specialized stroke rehabilitation programs
options.C: Routine immunization and growth monitoring
options.D: Occupational safety training for factory workers

explanation: Young children are most at risk for vaccine-preventable childhood illnesses and malnutrition, making immunization and growth monitoring top priorities. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h2)

question: Where is the median cubital vein located, which is a favourite spot for starting an IV?

options.A: Near the inside of the ankle joint
options.B: Along the lateral side of the upper arm
options.C: On the back of the hand
options.D: In the antecubital fossa of the elbow

explanation: Exactly! The median cubital vein sits right across the bend of the elbow (the antecubital fossa), making it super accessible for quick IV lines and blood tests.

question: Why is it important for nurses to know if a cancer treatment is meant to cure the disease or provide comfort (palliative)?

options.A: It dictates whether the patient is allowed to receive any form of nutrition by mouth
options.B: Palliative regimens mean the patient no longer requires physical assessments or lab work
options.C: Curative regimens require nurses to administer medications without checking vital signs
options.D: It helps guide realistic patient expectations, monitoring priorities, and supportive care planning

explanation: Great nursing insight! Knowing the main goal of treatment helps you plan the best supportive care and keep patient expectations clear and hopeful.

question: What hemoglobin level tells us a woman has anaemia during labor?

options.A: Below 14.5 g/dL
options.B: Below 11.0 g/dL
options.C: Below 12.5 g/dL
options.D: Below 10.0 g/dL

explanation: Great to know! The WHO sets 11.0 g/dL as the cutoff for pregnant and laboring women. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of passing an endotracheal tube during resuscitation?

options.A: To secure a direct passage for oxygen into the lungs
options.B: To remove fluid directly from the stomach
options.C: To prevent the patient from speaking to staff
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the patient

explanation: An endotracheal tube creates a safe, clear highway straight into the lungs, bypassing any blockages in the upper airway.

question: What is the main route of transmission for the pathogens that cause gastroenteritis?

options.A: Fecal-oral route
options.B: Broken skin contact
options.C: Direct droplet inhalation
options.D: Vector-borne mosquito bites

explanation: Gastroenteritis pathogens spread primarily when microscopic amounts of infected stool contaminate food, water, or hands and enter a new host's mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: What is a major drawback of relying too much on private healthcare in developing economies?

options.A: It forces public hospitals to close down due to lack of competition
options.B: It can exclude low-income earners who are unable to pay user fees
options.C: It provides free medical care to all citizens regardless of income
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for professional nursing staff

explanation: Private hospitals usually require cash upfront, locking out everyday citizens who rely on affordable public clinics. Access to health is a right!

question: What is the main reason nurses send a sample to the lab for a microbial culture?

options.A: To measure the exact number of red blood cells in circulation
options.B: To detect circulating antibodies produced by the patient's immune system
options.C: To grow and identify the specific microorganism causing the infection
options.D: To visualize stained tissue sections under a high-powered microscope

explanation: A culture gives germs a cozy place to multiply so the lab can figure out exactly what bug is making your patient sick.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical daytime sign of chronic insomnia?

options.A: Tension headaches
options.B: Poor memory and focus
options.C: Daytime fatigue and irritability
options.D: Improved cognitive concentration

explanation: Not that one! Lack of sleep definitely doesn't boost your brainpower. Instead, it leaves you feeling foggy, forgetful, and struggling to concentrate.

question: Why should the nurse encourage the patient to drink plenty of fluids after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To flush out remaining local anesthetic drugs
options.B: To prevent high blood pressure spikes
options.C: To keep the patient awake and alert
options.D: To help replace the lost cerebrospinal fluid

explanation: You got it! Fluids help the body quickly make up for the cerebrospinal fluid that was removed.

question: Why is it important to talk calmly with a nervous patient during an MRI scan?

options.A: To test if their cranial nerves are working
options.B: To distract them so they fall fast asleep
options.C: To keep their blood pressure high during the test
options.D: To reassure them and help them stay still so pictures aren't blurred

explanation: MRI machines are loud and tight spaces. A reassuring voice helps patients stay still so the images turn out clear.

question: How should you correctly measure the length of an infant?

options.A: Hanging suspended from a spring scale sling
options.B: Lying flat on a rigid length board with assistance
options.C: Using a flexible cloth tape measure on the bed
options.D: Standing upright against a wall stadiometer

explanation: Exactly! Babies can't stand yet, so we lay them flat on a length board to get a proper, reliable measurement.

question: Why is drama and local theatre such a hit when spreading health messages in rural communities?

options.A: They provide formal laboratory diagnosis for infectious diseases.
options.B: They use local arts and traditions that people already know and trust.
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak to patients directly.
options.D: They require expensive digital equipment and stable electricity.

explanation: People love stories and local culture! Using drama makes the community feel right at home and much more open to the health message.

question: What is the main cause of an ischemic stroke?

options.A: High pressure inside the skull
options.B: A ruptured blood vessel in the brain
options.C: A temporary lack of oxygen in the lungs
options.D: A blood clot blocking a brain vessel

explanation: Spot on! An ischemic stroke happens when something blocks blood flow in a brain vessel, cutting off oxygen. You've got this!

question: How do peer educators help drive the elimination of harmful practices at the village level?

options.A: By communicating health messages in relatable, culturally familiar ways
options.B: By performing surgical reversals of genital mutilation in homes
options.C: By issuing official fines to families who violate public health laws
options.D: By writing academic textbooks for university nursing students

explanation: Peers are trusted members of the community who can discuss sensitive topics without sounding judgmental or foreign. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h5)

question: Why would a doctor remove a small cervical polyp even if it isn't causing any symptoms?

options.A: To restore normal ovarian function
options.B: To stop potential future bleeding and permit testing
options.C: To prevent the spread of severe bacterial infection
options.D: To enlarge the cervical opening for childbirth

explanation: Taking it out stops random spotting before it starts and lets the lab test the tissue just to be completely safe.

question: What is the main goal of clinical assessment in palliative care?

options.A: To find a permanent cure for the disease
options.B: To shorten the overall length of hospital stay
options.C: To prove that medical treatments are failing
options.D: To maintain the best possible quality of life

explanation: In palliative care, we shift away from trying to cure and focus fully on keeping the patient as comfortable and happy as possible. You've got this!

question: A ward manager notices missed medication doses and sloppy handovers. What is the most likely underlying issue?

options.A: Low staff morale and diminished workplace motivation
options.B: An unexpected surplus of advanced diagnostic medical equipment
options.C: Excessively high patient satisfaction survey scores
options.D: Too many mandatory training workshops on patient empathy

explanation: When morale dips low, even simple daily routines like handovers can start slipping. Recognizing this helps us support one another better.

question: What is a major giveaway that a digital blood pressure cuff has an air leak?

options.A: The screen flashes bright red and rings a loud alarm
options.B: The battery icon shows full charge the whole time
options.C: The machine shows an error code or cannot finish pumping up
options.D: The device measures the blood pressure twice as fast as usual

explanation: If air is escaping, the machine can't build up the pressure it needs, so it will usually flash an error message at you.

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good evaluation?

options.A: Resistance to feedback
options.B: Rater bias and halo effects
options.C: Standardized grading rubrics
options.D: Severe time constraints

explanation: Rubrics actually fix evaluation problems by giving clear guidelines so grading is fair and consistent!

question: What is the main job of progesterone during the second half (luteal phase) of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: To trigger the initial onset of menstrual bleeding
options.B: To cause the breakdown of the corpus luteum
options.C: To prepare the uterine lining for a potential pregnancy
options.D: To stimulate the initial growth of ovarian follicles

explanation: Progesterone turns the inner walls of the womb (the endometrium) into a cozy, nutrient-rich bed, just in case a fertilized egg decides to implant.

question: What is the main goal of doing Leopold's maneuvers?

options.A: To measure the exact width of the maternal pelvis
options.B: To determine the position and presentation of the fetus
options.C: To check the rate of cervical dilation and effacement
options.D: To listen directly to the fetal heart sounds

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just systematic tummy checks to feel where the baby's head, back, and bottom are resting.

question: Which of these is usually the first noticeable sign that an adult is getting dehydrated?

options.A: Dark-colored urine
options.B: Swelling in the ankles
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Uncontrollable shaking

explanation: Spot on! When water is low, your kidneys hold onto as much fluid as they can, turning your urine a concentrated, dark yellow or brown.

question: Why is modern healthcare now encouraging fathers to get involved during pregnancy?

options.A: Government policies now fine fathers who stay away.
options.B: Women are no longer able to attend clinics alone.
options.C: Shared decision-making improves overall health outcomes.
options.D: Hospitals have extra space to accommodate couples.

explanation: When men are involved, health choices and money are planned together, leading to a healthier family! Keep it up.

question: In Vroom's expectancy theory, what does 'expectancy' actually mean?

options.A: The fear of being punished for a clinical error
options.B: The financial value attached to a year-end bonus
options.C: The belief that effort will lead to successful performance
options.D: The strict rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Correct! Expectancy is your personal belief that if you work hard, you will actually succeed at the task.

question: What is the best way to help a patient stick to their long-term blood pressure medication plan?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking pills whenever their blood pressure normalizes
options.B: Explaining that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it
options.C: Insisting that family members administer every daily dose orally
options.D: Warning the patient that stopping pills causes instant cardiac arrest

explanation: Fantastic! Patients often stop taking meds when they feel fine. Teaching them that the drugs are keeping their pressure under control helps them stay consistent for life.

question: What is the primary goal of health care financing in a population?

options.A: Mobilizing, pooling, and allocating funds for health services
options.B: Generating high profits for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Eliminating private hospitals from the healthcare market
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing training institutions

explanation: Health financing is fundamentally about gathering and distributing money to pay for needed health services. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h1)

question: How do school health programs help keep female students in class?

options.A: By strictly punishing any student who fails a monthly health examination
options.B: By managing hygiene, health screenings, and offering a safe support system
options.C: By providing free uniforms, books, and daily hot meals for all students
options.D: By taking over classroom teaching responsibilities from regular teachers

explanation: Correct! Providing clean facilities, health checks, and a listening ear helps girls feel safe, healthy, and confident to stay in school.

question: What do we really mean by 'motivation' when managing a nursing team?

options.A: The financial bonus given at the end of the year
options.B: The physical strength required to complete a shift
options.C: The internal drive that pushes a worker to take action
options.D: The strict set of rules enforced by the hospital board

explanation: Spot on! Motivation is that inner spark or energy that pushes us to chase our goals and get things done on the ward.

question: You need to help move a heavy patient up in bed. Which of these follows safe ergonomic practices?

options.A: Holding the patient far away from the body to keep uniform clean
options.B: Bending sharply at the waist with straight knees to gain momentum
options.C: Twisting the torso quickly while lifting to reach the bedside table
options.D: Using a mechanical lift or asking a colleague for assistance

explanation: Never try to be a lone hero with heavy lifting! Always ask a colleague to team-lift or use mechanical aids to protect your lower back.

question: Why are dietary fats considered energy-dense?

options.A: They contain no carbon or hydrogen atoms
options.B: They convert directly into muscle without breakdown
options.C: They are digested much faster than carbs
options.D: They supply more than double the calories per gram compared to carbs or protein

explanation: You've got this! Fats give you nine calories per gram, while proteins and carbs only give four. That means fats pack much more energy into a smaller amount.

question: Why is care in the emergency department prioritized based on severity instead of arrival time?

options.A: It is required by hospital administrative rules
options.B: Critically ill patients need immediate intervention to prevent death
options.C: First arrivals generally have minor complaints
options.D: Patients who arrive later usually pay higher fees

explanation: Triage ensures that those with life-threatening conditions receive immediate care regardless of when they walked through the door. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is avoiding all medications during pregnancy sometimes dangerous?

options.A: Untreated maternal health conditions can reduce oxygen and nutrients to the fetus
options.B: The placenta will release toxins if no drugs are present in the blood
options.C: Fetal organs will stop developing without chemical stimulation
options.D: Maternal hormones require medication to remain stable

explanation: Keeping the mother healthy is the best way to protect the baby. Uncontrolled sickness can starve the baby of vital oxygen and nutrients!

question: What happens when there is poor planning on a hospital ward?

options.A: An immediate surplus of protective equipment
options.B: Improved patient satisfaction scores
options.C: Shorter waiting times in emergency
options.D: Rushed medication rounds and exhausted nursing staff

explanation: Without a solid plan, the ward can quickly turn chaotic, leading to tired nurses and rushed care.

question: You visit a woman at 32 weeks who suddenly starts heavy vaginal bleeding. What should be your very first action?

options.A: Wait for her husband to return from work before acting
options.B: Tell her to rest until morning and monitor her
options.C: Ask her to walk around to encourage blood flow
options.D: Stabilize her condition and initiate emergency transport

explanation: Heavy bleeding late in pregnancy is a major emergency. Stabilize her as best as you can and get her moving to the hospital right away!

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard precaution practice?

options.A: Using a private negative-pressure room for every patient
options.B: Performing hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.C: Using safe injection practices and proper sharps disposal
options.D: Wearing gloves when touching non-intact skin or body fluids

explanation: Negative-pressure rooms are special transmission-based precautions for airborne germs, not a routine standard precaution for everyone. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h6)

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

options.A: Treating chronic adult diabetes mellitus
options.B: Scheduling permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Conducting forensic examinations for survivors of abuse
options.D: Screening for conditions like gestational hypertension

explanation: Great thinking! ANC visits give nurses a wonderful chance to monitor blood pressure and catch dangerous pregnancy complications early.

question: Why is talking about birth control options right after a medical abortion so important?

options.A: It stops abnormal uterine bleeding from starting.
options.B: It helps prevent rapid repeat unintended pregnancies.
options.C: It prevents the uterus from contracting too forcefully.
options.D: It ensures that fertility returns safely after six months.

explanation: You nailed it! Because ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion, discussing contraception early helps patients avoid unplanned pregnancies before they are ready.

question: What is an immediate, frontline nursing action when a patient expresses normal pregnancy ambivalence?

options.A: Validating feelings and normalizing the experience
options.B: Immediately prescribing high-dose antidepressant medications
options.C: Reporting the patient to child protective services
options.D: Advising the patient to stop attending antenatal clinics

explanation: You've got it! Letting mums know their mixed emotions are totally normal brings instant relief and builds trust.

question: Which of these is a very common anticholinergic anti-spasmodic drug you will see in the wards?

options.A: Bisacodyl
options.B: Omeprazole
options.C: Hyoscine butylbromide
options.D: Metoclopramide

explanation: Hyoscine butylbromide (often known by brand names like Buscopan) is a go-to medicine nurses give to help patients get fast relief from tummy cramps.

question: What is the antidote used in acute iron poisoning?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine sulfate
options.C: Protamine sulfate
options.D: Deferoxamine

explanation: Deferoxamine acts like a magnet, binding to excess iron in the blood so the kidneys can safely flush it out during an overdose.

question: Why is watching a patient's urine output so important after major pelvic surgery for cervical cancer?

options.A: Surgical dissection near the cervix can temporarily disrupt bladder nerve pathways
options.B: Patients are forbidden from drinking water for days after the operation
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs crystallize instantly inside the urinary bladder
options.D: The kidneys automatically shut down when the uterus is removed

explanation: Because the bladder nerves run very close to the womb, big surgeries can stun them temporarily, meaning the patient might need a catheter for a little while.

question: What does a null hypothesis usually claim?

options.A: There is no real difference or effect between the groups.
options.B: All patients in the sample will experience full recovery.
options.C: The new nursing intervention is better than the old one.
options.D: The study sample was too small to draw any conclusions.

explanation: You got it! The null hypothesis is like saying 'nothing special is happening here; any difference is just by chance.' It's the starting point for testing!

question: Why do we need a whole team (doctors, nurses, social workers) to plan for psychiatric parole?

options.A: Different experts cover medical, social, legal, and daily living needs.
options.B: It ensures that doctors make all decisions without input from other staff.
options.C: Courts legally require at least ten different signatures for a discharge.
options.D: It slows down the release process so patients stay in the hospital longer.

explanation: Exactly! Reintegrating into society isn't just about medicine; patients need help with housing, legal steps, and daily support, which takes a whole team.

question: How does blocking dopamine receptors help a patient taking a major tranquilizer?

options.A: It speeds up slow heart rates
options.B: It directly relieves acute muscle spasms
options.C: It reduces hallucinations and disorganized thinking
options.D: It lowers high blood pressure instantly

explanation: Too much dopamine activity can trigger psychotic symptoms. Blocking those receptors helps bring the patient back to a calm, clear reality.

question: When stepping into a patient's home for the very first time, how should a community nurse view their role?

options.A: As a temporary visitor with absolute control
options.B: As an authority figure inspecting domestic compliance
options.C: As an invited guest entering a personal space
options.D: As a casual observer with no clinical responsibility

explanation: Always remember you are entering someone's personal sanctuary. Treating yourself as an invited guest instantly shows respect and builds trust.

question: An environmental health officer is checking a suspected food poisoning outbreak at a local canteen. What is the very first step before any lab testing can start?

options.A: Collecting a representative sample using sterile equipment and proper cold storage
options.B: Immediately closing down all food businesses operating in that neighborhood
options.C: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all customers who ate at the canteen
options.D: Spraying chemical disinfectants across the entire kitchen and dining area

explanation: Brilliant! Lab tests are only as good as the sample you send them. Proper sterile collection and keeping it cold are always step one.

question: What is the primary function of leukocytes in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex carbohydrates in the gut
options.B: Regulating blood pressure and fluid balance
options.C: Defending the body against foreign invaders
options.D: Transporting oxygen to body tissues

explanation: Leukocytes are white blood cells whose main job is to recognize and destroy foreign pathogens like bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which blood test results confirm primary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum hormone
options.C: High serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and high parathyroid hormone

explanation: In primary hyperparathyroidism, an overactive gland pumps out too much PTH, which in turn drives your blood calcium levels way up.

question: What is the main goal of a community's 'production, distribution, and consumption' function?

options.A: Providing free hospital care to every citizen
options.B: Teaching cultural values to children in school buildings
options.C: Enforcing criminal laws and maintaining local police stations
options.D: Meeting the basic survival and economic needs of members

explanation: You've got it! This is simply about making sure people have access to food, shelter, and the basics needed to survive every day.

question: What was the main goal of classical management theory in the workplace?

options.A: Emotional counseling for all employees
options.B: Efficiency and standardized tasks
options.C: Flexible work hours and remote shifts
options.D: Democratic voting on all organizational policies

explanation: Classical management was all about maximum speed, clear chains of command, and doing tasks the exact same way every time like a machine.

question: Which of these drugs belongs to the methylxanthine family of bronchodilators?

options.A: Ipratropium
options.B: Salmeterol
options.C: Theophylline
options.D: Albuterol

explanation: Theophylline is a classic methylxanthine. Because it needs careful monitoring, it's a great drug to remember for your exams and clinical postings!

question: Which tool is commonly used in nursing education informatics to train students safely?

options.A: Hospital payroll and staff roster tracking spreadsheets
options.B: Barcode medication administration verification scanners
options.C: Patient simulation software and learning management systems
options.D: National public health disease outbreak registries

explanation: Educational informatics relies heavily on learning platforms and simulation tools to build student knowledge and skills. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional and religious leaders important in community mental health care?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nurses and social workers entirely
options.B: They provide the financial funding for all federal hospital budgets
options.C: They hold significant influence and can help mobilize the community against stigma
options.D: They are legally required to write official psychiatric prescriptions

explanation: Because many community members trust local and religious leaders, their involvement helps change negative attitudes and encourages families to seek help early. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which tool is best for giving a detailed, live look at heart valve movement and internal wall damage?

options.A: Bedside pulse oximetry
options.B: Routine blood chemistry panel
options.C: Echocardiogram
options.D: Standard chest X-ray

explanation: An echocardiogram uses sound waves (ultrasound) to let us see the heart valves and walls moving in real time. It's a powerful tool in cardiac care!

question: What makes NGOs so helpful when it comes to community food projects?

options.A: They possess unlimited financial budgets compared to national governments.
options.B: They rely exclusively on military force to secure food warehouses.
options.C: They can reach remote or marginalized populations that large governments often miss.
options.D: They have legal authority to write and pass new national laws.

explanation: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) are flexible and grassroots, meaning they can travel to tiny, hard-to-reach villages where big government programs rarely go.

question: Why don't we diagnose someone with high blood pressure (hypertension) after just one high reading?

options.A: Nigerian guidelines require at least five months of tracking
options.B: Blood pressure machines only work accurately on the third try
options.C: Systolic pressure changes constantly based on what food was eaten
options.D: Temporary factors like stress or rushing can falsely raise readings

explanation: Things like rushing to the clinic, traffic anxiety, or pain can make BP jump temporarily. That's why we always check a few times before making a diagnosis. Great job thinking like a nurse!

question: A nursing mum asks why her milk supply drops if she waits too long between feeds. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: Her breasts run out of physical space to store more fluid after a few hours
options.B: Infrequent suckling reduces prolactin surges and signals the body to slow production
options.C: The posterior pituitary gland stops working permanently after four hours of rest
options.D: Estrogen levels rise sharply every time the baby misses a scheduled feeding time

explanation: Spot on! Breastmilk works on a simple supply-and-demand rule. Less feeding means less hormone signaling, so the body makes less milk.

question: Which finding in a jaundiced newborn must be reported immediately because it points to bile duct disease?

options.A: Frequent crying during diaper changes
options.B: Clay-colored or pale stools
options.C: Yellow skin extending to the toes
options.D: Mild sleepiness between scheduled feeds

explanation: Stools that look pale or clay-colored mean bile isn't reaching the gut, which can signal a serious condition like biliary atresia. You are learning to spot the critical details!

question: What is a key clinical responsibility of a community health nurse managing tuberculosis (TB) patients?

options.A: Forcibly relocating infected families to urban centers
options.B: Supervising patients taking their medications daily (DOTS)
options.C: Manufacturing new antibiotics in a local laboratory
options.D: Performing major surgical operations on infected lungs

explanation: Wonderful! Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS) helps patients take every dose properly so the TB germ doesn't become drug-resistant.

question: Which nursing action helps thin thick respiratory secretions so they are easier for the patient to cough up?

options.A: Lying the patient flat on their back
options.B: Keeping the room air completely dry
options.C: Encouraging adequate daily fluid intake
options.D: Restricting all drinking water after meals

explanation: Drinking enough water keeps body fluids thin, which naturally loosens thick mucus in the respiratory tract. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why do nurses track balancing measures during an improvement project?

options.A: To detect any unintended negative consequences in other parts of the system
options.B: To compare the hospital performance against international standards
options.C: To balance the nursing unit's monthly financial budget and payroll
options.D: To ensure that doctors and nurses work the exact same number of hours

explanation: Brilliant! Balancing measures act like an early warning system to make sure fixing one problem doesn't accidentally cause another one somewhere else.

question: What is the main goal of managing an injured victim while they are inside a moving ambulance?

options.A: To complete all surgical procedures before hospital arrival
options.B: To prevent further injury and keep vital organs working
options.C: To diagnose the exact cause of the accident during transit
options.D: To discharge the patient home if vital signs stabilize

explanation: The transit phase focuses purely on stabilizing critical functions and protecting the patient from additional harm until they reach definitive care. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which part of the nephron features a dense brush border designed for heavy reabsorption?

options.A: Loop of Henle
options.B: Collecting duct
options.C: Proximal convoluted tubule
options.D: Distal convoluted tubule

explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined with microvilli that form a brush border, maximizing its ability to reabsorb nutrients and water from the filtrate. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h2)

question: What usually stops teenagers from visiting clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory free distribution of supplies in schools
options.B: A complete absence of hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Fear of being judged and a lack of privacy from staff
options.D: Strict laws requiring adolescent doctors for teenage patients

explanation: Teens often avoid seeking help because they are scared healthcare workers will gossip, judge them, or break their trust. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to understand basic legal frameworks regarding harmful practices?

options.A: To recognize mandatory reporting duties and protect vulnerable patients
options.B: To arrest individuals who bring injured patients to the hospital
options.C: To write new bills for the national legislative assembly
options.D: To act as defense attorneys during court trials for offenders

explanation: Nurses must know when the law requires reporting child abuse or imminent danger to child protection authorities. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h3)

question: What are small pieces of digital data called when they travel across a network?

options.A: Pixels
options.B: Packets
options.C: Pulses
options.D: Plugs

explanation: Data is broken down into small units known as packets so it can travel efficiently across computer networks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which situation can instantly plunge a family into a deep emotional crisis?

options.A: Attending a community health talk
options.B: Going for a routine yearly check-up at the clinic
options.C: Learning how to take home medications properly
options.D: A main breadwinner getting hit with a serious, long-term illness

explanation: When unexpected illness strikes the person providing for the home, it shatters family stability and money security all at once.

question: Which of the following organs is NOT typically considered a primary target organ damaged by long-term hypertension?

options.A: Brain
options.B: Kidneys
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Heart

explanation: The primary target organs damaged by chronic high blood pressure are the heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h7)

question: Which sign is a clinical indicator of severe respiratory distress in an adult patient?

options.A: Relaxed posture in a flat bed
options.B: Slow and deep regular breathing
options.C: Use of accessory neck muscles
options.D: Warm and pink skin coloration

explanation: When breathing becomes very hard, patients use their neck and chest muscles to help force air in and out. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h3)

question: A fully awake and clear-headed patient says 'No' to a painful procedure. Which ethical principle supports their choice?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy gives every adult patient the right to self-determination. They own their body, so they get to accept or reject medical treatments based on what matters to them.

question: Where is the gray matter located in the cross-section of the spinal cord?

options.A: Directly outside the dura mater
options.B: Inside the central canal fluid
options.C: On the outer surface as tracts
options.D: On the inside in an H-shape

explanation: Unlike the brain where gray matter is on the outside, the spinal cord places its gray matter on the inside surrounded by white matter. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is a case definition used for during an outbreak?

options.A: To close down international borders during a viral infection
options.B: To prescribe the exact dosage of antibiotics a patient must receive
options.C: To determine how much financial compensation a sick worker gets
options.D: To apply standard criteria so everyone counts the same illness cases accurately

explanation: A case definition is like a checklist. It gives all health workers a uniform way to decide if someone truly has the outbreak disease.

question: How many months in a row without a period does a woman need to confirm she has reached menopause?

options.A: Six consecutive months
options.B: Twenty-four consecutive months
options.C: Twelve consecutive months
options.D: Three consecutive months

explanation: To be sure the monthly cycle has stopped for good, doctors look for a full year (12 months) of no menstruation. You've got this!

question: What happens to carbon dioxide during gas exchange in the lungs?

options.A: It moves from the pulmonary capillaries into the alveoli
options.B: It combines with oxygen to form a new nutrient compound
options.C: It binds tightly to hemoglobin inside the red blood cells
options.D: It is actively pumped from the alveoli into the bloodstream

explanation: Carbon dioxide travels from the blood in the capillaries across the membrane into the air sacs so it can leave the body through exhalation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why do hospitals prefer Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) over handwriting prescriptions on paper?

options.A: It allows nurses to change medication dosages without a doctor's approval
options.B: It ensures that clients never experience side effects from medications
options.C: It eliminates dangerous transcription errors caused by messy handwriting
options.D: It speeds up the physical manufacturing of pills in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Typed orders mean no more guessing what a doctor wrote, preventing mistakes from unclear handwriting or confusing abbreviations. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: Pick's disease mainly affects which areas of the brain first?

options.A: Frontal and temporal lobes
options.B: Occipital and parietal lobes
options.C: Thalamus and hypothalamus
options.D: Cerebellum and brainstem

explanation: Pick's disease zeroes in on the frontal and temporal parts of the brain, which handle our personality, behavior, and language. Spotting this early helps you understand why patients act differently long before memory issues start!

question: Why do we give emergency epinephrine into the thigh muscle instead of the arm?

options.A: The drug is absorbed much faster into the bloodstream from the thigh
options.B: The skin on the thigh feels less pain
options.C: Arm muscles are too small for emergency drugs
options.D: It stops the patient from seeing the needle

explanation: The vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh has great blood flow, helping the epinephrine get to work as fast as possible when every second counts.

question: What structural feature makes capillaries ideally suited for gas and nutrient exchange?

options.A: They are equipped with one-way valves to prevent backflow
options.B: Their walls are only a single cell layer thick
options.C: They contain strong layers of circular smooth muscle
options.D: Their lumen has a larger diameter than any other vessel

explanation: Having a wall thickness of just one cell minimizes the diffusion distance for oxygen, nutrients, and waste products. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the scientific term used for parasitic worms in medical practice?

options.A: Bacteroids
options.B: Protozoa
options.C: Helminths
options.D: Mycoses

explanation: Helminths is the broad biological term used to describe parasitic worms that infect humans and animals. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the difference between anonymity and confidentiality?

options.A: Anonymity means no one can link data to a name; confidentiality keeps known identities secret
options.B: Anonymity is optional in nursing research; confidentiality is strictly mandatory
options.C: Anonymity applies only to secondary data; confidentiality applies to primary data
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical research studies

explanation: Anonymity means nobody (not even the researcher) knows whose data is whose. Confidentiality means you know who they are, but you keep their identity locked away safe.

question: What is the most important thing for a nurse to check right after giving a nebulizer treatment with a beta-agonist?

options.A: Checking the patient for signs of severe weight gain
options.B: Reassessing lung sounds and respiratory effort
options.C: Offering the patient a heavy, high-sodium meal
options.D: Inspecting the skin for signs of bruising or rashes

explanation: Always close the loop! Listening to the patient's lungs afterward lets you know right away if the medication did its job and made breathing easier.

question: What is most likely to happen if a new DRF launches with too little seed capital?

options.A: Patients will receive completely free medications for life
options.B: The government will stop taxing local pharmaceutical companies
options.C: The pharmacy will experience immediate stock-outs due to low inventory
options.D: The facility will automatically make massive profits in the first week

explanation: Spot on! If you start with too little inventory, you can't meet patient needs, and the system stalls before it even really begins.

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you realize you made a medication error?

options.A: Hide the medication chart so visitors do not notice the mistake
options.B: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide necessary care
options.C: Blame the pharmacy department for supplying the wrong dose
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to mention it during handover

explanation: Patient safety always comes first. Check your patient's vital signs and status immediately so you can handle any issues right away.

question: What is a main benefit of having several alcohol-free days each week?

options.A: To completely reverse any genetic predisposition to liver failure
options.B: To double the recommended intake limits on the remaining days
options.C: To ensure the body stores enough pure ethanol for energy
options.D: To prevent tolerance buildup and lower the risk of dependency

explanation: Giving the liver and the habit a break helps prevent your body from getting too used to daily alcohol. It's a great way to keep drinking habits in check!

question: Why is it important to involve bedside nurses when drafting clinical standards?

options.A: They perform the actual care and understand practical floor realities
options.B: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase
options.C: It removes the need for any supervisory oversight
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to sign administrative policies

explanation: Frontline nurses know what works in daily practice, making their input vital for creating realistic and usable standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why does a woman with an infibulated scar have a higher risk of prolonged labor?

options.A: The fetus grows at an abnormally fast rate
options.B: The scar tissue is rigid and blocks normal stretching of the birth canal
options.C: Contractions of the uterus are completely paralyzed
options.D: The placenta attaches directly to the scar tissue

explanation: Correct! Dense scar tissue lacks elasticity, acting as a physical wall that stops the baby from descending smoothly during birth. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why must you always lock your computer screen when walking away from the nurses' station?

options.A: To prevent the central processing unit from overheating during idle times
options.B: To automatically save any unsaved nursing notes to the cloud
options.C: To save electrical power and extend the lifespan of the monitor display
options.D: To protect patient privacy and prevent unauthorized access to health records

explanation: Leaving a screen unlocked risks patient confidentiality. A quick lock keeps sensitive health records safe from prying eyes!

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean for caregivers of patients with degenerative illnesses?

options.A: Grief felt in advance as they watch their loved one slowly decline
options.B: Anger at the medical team for failing to find a genetic cure
options.C: Relief that the patient's physical illness will soon be over
options.D: Confusion about how to fill out insurance and hospital forms

explanation: Spot on. Caregivers often mourn the gradual loss of their loved one's personality and skills long before the person actually passes away. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)

question: Why do malnutrition and chronic infections often trap people in a vicious cycle?

options.A: Vitamins can only be absorbed if a person has a chronic parasite.
options.B: Infections cause permanent brain damage that stops people from eating.
options.C: Malnutrition weakens immunity, and infections worsen nutritional status.
options.D: Malnutrition prevents antibiotics from working inside the stomach.

explanation: You've got it! Poor nutrition lowers your defense against sickness, and being sick robs your body of nutrients—each one feeds the other.

question: Which type of patient needs a full-body mechanical lift?

options.A: An ambulatory patient who walks with a cane
options.B: A patient who only needs a gentle reminder to stand
options.C: A restless patient who tries to jump out of bed
options.D: A completely dependent patient who cannot bear weight

explanation: If a patient has zero weight-bearing ability, a mechanical lift does the heavy lifting safely for both you and the patient.

question: Why is a proper verbal and written handover necessary when bringing a patient to a new ward?

options.A: To prevent family members from asking questions about the bill
options.B: To satisfy insurance companies that the trip took place
options.C: To give the transport nurse an excuse to leave the hospital early
options.D: To ensure continuity of safe care and prevent important details from being lost

explanation: Exactly! A solid handover bridges the gap between transport and the new ward, keeping patient safety front and center.

question: A patient asks why her body doesn't reject the developing pregnancy as a foreign object. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: The baby carries the exact same blood type as the mother always
options.B: The placenta completely blocks all maternal blood cells from forming
options.C: The mother's immune system shuts down completely during pregnancy
options.D: The outer trophoblast layer actively modifies local immune responses

explanation: The placenta and outer cells are clever—they whisper to the immune system to stay calm so the baby can grow safely. Clinical communication made simple!

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient NOT to squeeze their buttocks while doing Kegels?

options.A: To avoid raising the patient's blood pressure
options.B: To ensure the correct pelvic floor muscles are being isolated
options.C: To prevent cramping in the leg muscles
options.D: To keep the bladder from emptying too quickly

explanation: Brilliant! Squeezing the glutes or thighs cheats the exercise. We want the actual pelvic sling doing the heavy lifting!

question: What is the best immediate nursing action for an unconscious patient who is breathing on their own?

options.A: Force fluids by mouth to prevent dehydration during sleep
options.B: Place them in the recovery position to keep the airway clear
options.C: Prop them upright in bed to encourage deep lung breathing
options.D: Tie their arms to the bed rails to prevent sudden movement

explanation: The recovery position keeps the tongue from blocking the airway and lets saliva drain out safely. A classic life-saving nursing skill!

question: What hollow tube is formed when the edges of the neural plate fold and fuse together?

options.A: Neural tube
options.B: Neural crest
options.C: Amniotic sac
options.D: Notochord

explanation: Great job! The folding and closing of the neural plate forms the hollow neural tube, which eventually becomes our central nervous system.

question: Which term describes a histogram where the left and right sides mirror each other around a center peak?

options.A: Right-skewed distribution
options.B: Bimodal split distribution
options.C: Bell-shaped distribution
options.D: Left-skewed distribution

explanation: Think of a church bell! A symmetrical, bell-shaped curve means your data is nicely balanced around the average.

question: Why is it important for home health nurses to check in on the family caregiver's health too?

options.A: If the caregiver falls ill, the entire home care arrangement can collapse.
options.B: Caregivers are legally responsible for writing medical prescriptions.
options.C: Family members are the primary patients receiving nursing therapy.
options.D: Hospital regulations require checking caregiver blood pressure weekly.

explanation: Spot on! The patient's safety at home relies heavily on the health and well-being of the person taking care of them.

question: What is the main danger of polycythemia vera (a condition where the body makes too many blood cells)?

options.A: Hyperviscosity and abnormal clot formation
options.B: Massive platelet destruction and bleeding
options.C: Severe iron deficiency and rapid hemolysis
options.D: Total bone marrow aplasia and infection

explanation: When you have too many cells packed into the blood, it gets thick and sludgy (hyperviscosity). This makes dangerous blood clots much more likely to form.

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'food supply'?

options.A: The exact number of calories a single person eats daily
options.B: The specific diet chosen by individual families at home
options.C: The total amount of food produced and made available in a region
options.D: The amount of money budgeted for grocery shopping

explanation: Food supply is simply about the total food available through farming, storage, and trade across a whole area. You've got this!

question: Where should a completed incident report be submitted in the hospital?

options.A: Pinned to the public notice board in the main nursing station
options.B: Glued permanently inside the front cover of the patient's bedside chart
options.C: Mailed straight to the national nursing council office
options.D: Submitted directly to the quality or risk management department

explanation: That's right! Incident reports go straight to risk management or quality units, keeping them separate from the patient's clinical bedside chart.

question: What is dyspareunia, a common complaint among FGM survivors?

options.A: Severe fear of hospital environments
options.B: Chronic swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Inability to produce breast milk
options.D: Painful sexual intercourse

explanation: Dyspareunia simply means persistent pain during sex, usually resulting from severe scarring and nerve damage. Knowing this helps you support your patients better!

question: What part of the communication loop lets the nurse know if the client understood the message?

options.A: Sender
options.B: Channel
options.C: Interference
options.D: Feedback

explanation: Feedback is the response given by the receiver, which tells the nurse whether the message was clearly understood. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: What is the main job of the human immune system?

options.A: To tell the difference between the body's own cells and foreign substances
options.B: To break down food and absorb nutrients
options.C: To filter liquid waste from the bloodstream
options.D: To pump oxygen-rich blood to body tissues

explanation: Think of the immune system as the body's security guard. Its core job is to recognize foreign invaders while making sure it leaves your body's own healthy tissues alone!

question: Which online database is built specifically for nursing and allied health literature?

options.A: Lexicomp
options.B: Wikipedia
options.C: Google Drive
options.D: CINAHL

explanation: Spot on! CINAHL is every nursing student's best friend for finding trusted nursing journals and research.

question: What is the key job of the special fluid called surfactant in your lungs?

options.A: To reduce surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse
options.B: To bind oxygen molecules directly for transport
options.C: To moisten the trachea and primary bronchi
options.D: To trap dust and bacteria entering the deep lungs

explanation: Brilliant! Surfactant keeps the tiny air sacs from sticking together and collapsing on themselves when you breathe out.

question: What is the main danger of a massive, uncontrolled bleed?

options.A: It drops blood volume and stops oxygen flow to organs
options.B: It blocks normal clotting completely
options.C: It triggers overproduction of red blood cells
options.D: It causes an immediate spike in blood pressure

explanation: When too much blood is lost, there isn't enough volume left to pump oxygen to vital organs, which can lead to shock. Great job thinking through patient safety!

question: Why is the adhesive tape test preferred over a regular stool sample for diagnosing pinworms?

options.A: Stool samples destroy pinworm eggs due to high digestive enzyme levels
options.B: Stool microscopy cannot detect any form of nematode whatsoever
options.C: Pinworm larvae hatch instantly once they come into contact with water
options.D: Female pinworms lay eggs on the perianal skin rather than inside the feces

explanation: Since pinworms lay their eggs outside the bowels on the skin around the anus, regular stool tests usually miss them. That's why the tape test works best!

question: What is a main characteristic of primary health care?

options.A: It is delivered solely by medical specialists inside tertiary hospitals
options.B: It is restricted only to wealthy individuals with private health insurance
options.C: It provides universally accessible and affordable care to the community
options.D: It focuses exclusively on expensive surgical procedures in capital cities

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be universally accessible, affordable, and acceptable to all members of the community. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is the cortical reaction important right when fertilization happens?

options.A: It prevents more than one sperm from entering the egg
options.B: It helps the fertilized egg travel down the fallopian tube
options.C: It provides extra energy for the newly formed zygote
options.D: It speeds up the process of genetic material fusion

explanation: Once the first lucky sperm gets inside, the egg quickly changes its outer coat to lock out all other sperm. It's like a VIP bouncer keeping things orderly!

question: What is a great way to keep a multisectoral team accountable and working well together?

options.A: Holding meetings only once every five years to review old records
options.B: Leaving each sector to work completely independently without reporting back
options.C: Establishing joint monitoring committees with representatives from all involved sectors
options.D: Allowing the health ministry to make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Correct! Joint committees help everyone stay on the same page, track shared goals, and solve problems as a team.

question: A nurse agrees to perform a 'mild' form of FGM in a private clinic to save a young girl from a harsher traditional cut. What could happen to this nurse?

options.A: A minor warning from the local hospital management board
options.B: Loss of nursing license, fines, and criminal imprisonment
options.C: Promotion for successfully reducing community health risks
options.D: Mandatory attendance at a cultural sensitivity workshop

explanation: Exactly. Doing FGM in a clinic doesn't protect a nurse from the law—it is still a serious crime that leads to jail time and losing your license.

question: A hospital audit reveals that half of all postpartum women did not receive timely blood pressure checks. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Hide the report so the hospital management does not get angry
options.B: Share the feedback with the nurses and retrain staff on monitoring
options.C: Blame individual patients for refusing their vital signs checks
options.D: Stop taking blood pressures entirely to save nursing time

explanation: Audit results must be used to provide feedback and education to correct gaps in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why do nurses often treat life threats at the exact same time they assess the patient in an emergency?

options.A: Because hospital regulations require double documentation for all tasks
options.B: Because doctors prefer to delegate all physical tasks to students
options.C: Because waiting to treat life threats while finishing an assessment can be fatal
options.D: Because nurses have too much free time during shifts

explanation: In critical care, assessment and treatment happen together. A dying patient cannot wait for a slow, complete exam!

question: How do traditional healthcare systems generally view the concept of healing?

options.A: As a holistic experience involving body, mind, and spirit
options.B: As a scientific procedure performed only in laboratories
options.C: As a purely physical process involving only medication
options.D: As a temporary distraction from real psychological issues

explanation: Spot on! Traditional systems look at the whole person—including their spiritual wellbeing and community ties—rather than just physical symptoms.

question: How is disaster nursing different from regular hospital nursing?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for proper patient documentation
options.B: It shifts focus from single patients to community-wide health needs
options.C: It relies entirely on advanced surgical procedures in the field
options.D: It allows nurses to ignore standard infection control practices

explanation: While everyday nursing hones in on the individual at the bedside, disaster nursing zooms out to protect the health of the whole community.

question: Why are the axillary lymph nodes so important when checking a patient for breast lumps?

options.A: They help fight off skin infections.
options.B: They supply primary blood flow to the nipple.
options.C: They control milk production in the alveoli.
options.D: They are the main path for spreading breast cancer cells.

explanation: Great job thinking critically! Since most breast lymph fluid drains straight to the armpit, nurses always check the axillary lymph nodes first for signs of cancer spread.

question: What is the correct way to use an alcohol hand rub after pumping it onto your hands?

options.A: Blow on the hands to speed up the evaporation process
options.B: Rub all hand surfaces together until the alcohol dries completely
options.C: Wipe the hands dry immediately with a cotton towel
options.D: Rinse the excess gel off under running water

explanation: Keep rubbing all parts of your hands until the gel dries completely—that's when you know it has done its job of killing the germs.

question: Early-onset conduct disorder in childhood is a major risk factor for which adult mental health condition?

options.A: Parkinson's disease
options.B: Alzheimer's dementia
options.C: Antisocial personality disorder
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder

explanation: Severe conduct problems that begin early in life can unfortunately persist into adulthood as antisocial personality patterns if not addressed.

question: Why does the idea of 'agency' matter when you are carrying out your daily nursing duties?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change hospital policies without approval.
options.B: It means the nurse is personally exempt from all criminal laws.
options.C: It binds the hospital principal for acts done within employment scope.
options.D: It transfers complete medical licensing rights to the institution.

explanation: As a nurse acting within your normal duties, you represent the hospital. That means your professional actions on the job legally involve the hospital as your principal. Simple and clear!

question: Why is it important to have extra pediatric or neonatal staff in the delivery room for a twin birth?

options.A: Hospital policy mandates double documentation for all births.
options.B: Each baby may require immediate assessment and potential resuscitation.
options.C: The mother requires two separate anesthetists during surgery.
options.D: Twins are always born with identical congenital heart defects.

explanation: Spot on! Multiples are more likely to arrive early or feel stressed during birth, so having extra neonatal hands ready for every baby is always a smart and safe plan.

question: What is the key difference between active and passive infection surveillance?

options.A: Active surveillance only occurs at night, while passive surveillance happens during morning shifts
options.B: Active surveillance involves staff proactively hunting for data, while passive relies on voluntary reporting
options.C: Passive surveillance tracks viral illnesses, while active surveillance focuses only on bacterial issues
options.D: Passive surveillance uses computer software, while active surveillance is done entirely on paper

explanation: Spot on! Active means staff actively go looking for cases, while passive means waiting for someone to report them.

question: A patient is drowsy and can only be woken up when you apply strong, painful physical stimuli. What is this level of consciousness called?

options.A: Lethargy
options.B: Obtundation
options.C: Confusion
options.D: Stupor

explanation: When a patient is in a stupor, they are deeply asleep or unresponsive, and it takes strong physical prodding to get them to react. You've got this!

question: Where in the body are the main arterial pressure sensors (baroreceptors) located?

options.A: Pulmonary veins and left ventricle
options.B: Renal cortex and medullary pyramids
options.C: Carotid sinuses and aortic arch
options.D: Right atrium and superior vena cava

explanation: The body keeps tabs on blood pressure using special stretch sensors placed right near the brain's highway (carotid sinuses) and the main exit from the heart (aortic arch).

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to cause a slow resting heart rate (bradycardia)?

options.A: Acute high fever
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Hypothyroidism
options.D: Hyperthyroidism

explanation: An underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) slows down the body's overall metabolism, which often leads to a slower resting heart rate.

question: What do we call the large amount of urine passed in the first few days after having a baby?

options.A: Tubular necrosis
options.B: Glomerular shutdown
options.C: Postpartum diuresis
options.D: Renal exhaustion

explanation: Postpartum diuresis is just the body's way of getting rid of all that extra pregnancy fluid it doesn't need anymore. Frequent trips to the bathroom are expected!

question: Which piece of bedside equipment is a must-have when giving mouth care to an unresponsive patient?

options.A: Hard wooden tongue blades
options.B: A sharp dental mirror probe
options.C: Working suction machine
options.D: Strong alcoholic mouthwash

explanation: Unconscious patients can't spit or swallow water on their own. Having a suction machine ready is vital to clear out liquids and prevent choking.

question: Why do public health nurses look at mental health through a collective lens rather than just an individual one?

options.A: A person's state of mind is deeply connected to their environment and living conditions
options.B: Individual therapy sessions are too expensive for community clinics to fund
options.C: Group counseling is the only proven method to treat depression
options.D: Government policies require nurses to ignore personal medical histories

explanation: Because people are influenced by their surroundings, housing, and social networks, community nurses must evaluate the broader environment to understand mental well-being. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of giving a daily bed bath to a very ill patient?

options.A: Providing gentle touch and comfort to the patient
options.B: Permanently curing chronic underlying heart disease
options.C: Removing sweat and bacteria from the skin surface
options.D: Allowing the nurse to inspect the skin for early redness

explanation: Bed baths are amazing for hygiene, comfort, and skin checks, but they unfortunately can't fix chronic internal conditions like heart disease.

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why local women rarely attend hypertension screening camps. What is the best initial action?

options.A: Close the screening camp and open a men's health clinic
options.B: Report the community to the ministry of health immediately
options.C: Assume women do not care about their heart health
options.D: Hold focus groups with local women to discuss their barriers

explanation: Engaging directly with the affected population through focus groups uncovers the real reasons behind low attendance. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h7)

question: What is the typical time frame for an immediate drug reaction to appear after administration?

options.A: Within minutes to a few hours
options.B: Only upon stopping the drug
options.C: Between three and seven days
options.D: After two weeks of treatment

explanation: Immediate reactions happen very quickly, usually within minutes up to a few hours after the medication enters the body. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h1)

question: A nurse is preparing to care for a patient with an airborne infection. What must be done before entering the room to ensure effective PPE use?

options.A: Ask another staff member to hold their breath for them
options.B: Rely on natural room ventilation to clean the air
options.C: Wear any old pair of cloth gloves found in the utility room
options.D: Select the correct respirator mask and check its fit and seal

explanation: Proper PPE selection and fit checking are essential to ensure the equipment actually blocks the airborne hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary responsibility of the team leader during a cardiac arrest?

options.A: Performing all chest compressions without ever taking a break
options.B: Inserting all advanced airway tubes and starting peripheral IVs
options.C: Drawing up every emergency medication personally at the bedside
options.D: Overseeing the overall resuscitation and guiding clear role assignments

explanation: The leader coordinates the team's actions from a big-picture view rather than getting trapped in single tasks. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h8)

question: Why would a nurse researcher choose a cross-sectional design?

options.A: To find out how many people currently have a specific health issue
options.B: To test the long-term effects of a new surgical procedure
options.C: To track how a chronic illness changes in a patient from childhood to old age
options.D: To prove that one specific drug directly cures a disease over time

explanation: This design is your go-to when you want a quick snapshot of how common a health issue is right now in your community.

question: What does a positive alkaline phosphatase test in a milk sample tell you?

options.A: The milk is completely sterile and safe to drink
options.B: The milk has been stored at freezing temperatures
options.C: Antibiotics were successfully added to the batch
options.D: Pasteurization was incomplete or inadequate

explanation: You're learning fast! Alkaline phosphatase is a natural enzyme that proper pasteurization destroys. If it's still active in the test, the milk wasn't heated correctly.

question: Why must nurses apply lubricating eye drops to an unconscious patient who cannot close their eyelids?

options.A: To test the corneal blink reflex every hour
options.B: To prevent corneal drying, ulceration, and infection
options.C: To decrease pressure inside the eyeball
options.D: To stimulate the optic nerve and improve brain activity

explanation: Spot on! Without natural blinking, the eye surface dries out quickly, so artificial tears protect the eyes from painful ulcers.

question: What does the systolic blood pressure reading measure?

options.A: The pressure when the heart rests
options.B: The total volume of blood in the body
options.C: The pressure when the heart beats
options.D: The speed of blood flow in veins

explanation: Systolic pressure represents the force in the arteries when the heart muscle contracts to pump blood forward. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h1)

question: What treatment involves placing tiny radioactive sources directly inside or close to a cervical tumor?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Cryotherapy
options.C: Brachytherapy
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: You've got it! 'Brachy' means close—so brachytherapy places radiation right next to or inside the tumor to target bad cells while sparing healthy tissue.

question: Why do lung problems often affect the rest of the body?

options.A: Lung infections spread directly to the brain within hours
options.B: Every organ relies heavily on a steady supply of oxygen from the lungs
options.C: Poor breathing causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely
options.D: The heart stops pumping blood when the lungs become inflamed

explanation: You got it! If the lungs aren't working well, oxygen delivery drops, and every single tissue in the body starts to suffer. Oxygen is food for our cells!

question: What was the main lesson learned from early public health nursing pioneers like Florence Nightingale?

options.A: Hospitals must be built larger to isolate sick people from healthy relatives
options.B: Clean environments and sanitation significantly reduce disease and death rates
options.C: Nurses should only practice inside sterile operating rooms and clinics
options.D: Herbal remedies are always superior to manufactured pharmaceuticals

explanation: Early pioneers proved that environmental conditions and sanitation are directly linked to community health and survival. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h2)

question: What does the acronym ISBAR stand for in emergency handover communication?

options.A: Investigation, Symptoms, Bleeding, Airway, Respiration
options.B: Introduction, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Injury, Status, Breathing, Access, Response
options.D: Immediate, Safety, Blood pressure, Assessment, Recovery

explanation: ISBAR is a standardized communication tool used by healthcare providers to ensure accurate and concise patient handovers. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h8)

question: What are the three main building blocks of healthcare financing?

options.A: Revenue collection, risk pooling, and purchasing
options.B: Drug manufacturing, supply, and distribution
options.C: Budgeting, staffing, and facility management
options.D: Patient admission, treatment, and discharge

explanation: Think of healthcare financing like a cooperative thrift society: you collect money, pool the risk together, and buy what the group needs. These three steps keep health systems running!

question: What is the main goal of doing an anthropometric assessment in nursing?

options.A: Measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the body
options.B: Assessing neurological reflexes and sensory function
options.C: Evaluating electrical activity within the heart muscle
options.D: Analyzing blood chemistry and electrolyte levels

explanation: You got this! Anthropometry is all about checking physical dimensions like height, weight, and skinfolds to see how healthy and well-nourished someone is.

question: What is the very first thing that happens during the initiation phase of cancer development?

options.A: The immune system completely destroys the mutated cell
options.B: New blood vessels sprout to feed the growing tumor mass
options.C: Abnormal cells spread through blood to distant organs
options.D: Permanent damage or mutation happens to the cell DNA

explanation: Initiation is the starting spark—it's that first permanent hit or change to the cell's DNA caused by a carcinogen.

question: Which method is commonly used to find out about past exposures in a case-control study?

options.A: Surgical intervention
options.B: Randomized clinical trials
options.C: Direct laboratory observation of future events
options.D: Interviews and questionnaires

explanation: Spot on! Since we are looking backward, we rely heavily on talking to patients and reviewing their past records using questionnaires and interviews.

question: What major economic challenge often pushes desperate families toward child traffickers?

options.A: Widespread poverty and lack of basic needs
options.B: Abundant job opportunities in local markets
options.C: Strict government taxes on large families
options.D: Excessive wealth in rural farming villages

explanation: When families struggle to put food on the table, traffickers easily trick parents by promising money or a better future for their kids.

question: What is the biggest downside or risk linked to the intraperitoneal route?

options.A: High risk of infection and peritonitis
options.B: Complete failure of the human respiratory system
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Instantaneous destruction of all oral medications

explanation: You got it! Anytime you open up or access the sterile peritoneal cavity, germs can sneak in, making infection and peritonitis the main danger to watch for. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's food intake?

options.A: It relies heavily on the patient's memory
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment
options.C: It only measures water and ignores solid food
options.D: It takes over three hours to complete

explanation: Patients easily forget small snacks or misjudge portion sizes when trying to remember everything they ate yesterday.

question: A client with a very irregular period asks to use the standard calendar method. What should you tell her as a nurse?

options.A: Reassure her that calendar tracking works best with irregular periods
options.B: Instruct her to double the length of her bleeding days
options.C: Advise her that irregular cycles make the calendar method unreliable
options.D: Tell her to simply use day 14 as her only unsafe day
