explanation: The calendar method needs predictable cycle lengths. When cycles bounce around unpredictably, it's very hard to guess the fertile window using math alone.

question: How do you place AED pads on a patient who has a pacemaker lump on their upper left chest?

options.A: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from the device
options.B: Refuse to use the AED because implanted devices block shocks entirely
options.C: Disable the pacemaker using a magnet before applying the pads
options.D: Place the AED pad directly over the bulge to improve shock delivery

explanation: Just place the pad about an inch away from the pacemaker bulge. If you put it right on top, it can absorb the shock energy and damage the implanted device.

question: Why is relying only on the average (mean) value of patient data sometimes tricky?

options.A: It is always mathematically incorrect to use averages in healthcare research
options.B: It completely hides the most common value in the distribution
options.C: It changes based on the total number of patients in the study
options.D: It does not show how spread out or inconsistent the individual readings are

explanation: Averages can hide the whole story! Two wards might have the same average temperature, but one ward has everyone very stable while the other has wild highs and lows.

question: What is the collective term for all the external structures of the female reproductive system?

options.A: Vestibule
options.B: Vulva
options.C: Perineum
options.D: Introitus

explanation: The vulva is the medical term used to describe all the external female genital structures combined. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h1)

question: A nurse is examining a child with suspected paralytic polio. What is a key physical sign to look for?

options.A: Gradual ascending paralysis starting in the feet
options.B: Painful joint swelling and localized skin rashes
options.C: Symmetrical rigid spasms and hyperactive reflexes
options.D: Asymmetrical muscle weakness and absent reflexes

explanation: Well done! Polio typically causes floppy weakness on one side more than the other (asymmetrical) along with missing reflexes in those limbs.

question: What is the main goal of Psychological First Aid (PFA) right after a disaster?

options.A: Forcing victims to recount every painful detail of the event
options.B: Providing humane practical support and reducing immediate distress
options.C: Conducting deep psychoanalysis to cure chronic personality disorders
options.D: Prescribing high-dose psychiatric medications to every survivor

explanation: You got this! PFA is all about offering a comforting presence, safety, and practical help—not forcing people into heavy therapy right away.

question: Which leadership style uses a system of rewards and punishments to manage staff?

options.A: Authentic leadership
options.B: Situational leadership
options.C: Transformational leadership
options.D: Transactional leadership

explanation: Think 'transaction'—you do this task well, you get rewarded; you make a mistake, you face correction. That's transactional leadership!

question: A patient chooses a private hospital over a public teaching hospital to avoid long queues. What does this show?

options.A: Mandatory community health outreach
options.B: Dependence on federal tax subsidies
options.C: Exclusively preventive health programming
options.D: Responsiveness to consumer preferences

explanation: Private facilities want to keep clients happy, so they often focus on faster service and comfort to match what patients are looking for.

question: Why do many Nigerian patients choose private health facilities even though they must pay cash out of pocket?

options.A: They often perceive private care to have better quality and shorter waiting times
options.B: Private hospitals offer free medications to every registered citizen
options.C: Private clinics are entirely subsidized by federal government revenue
options.D: The law forbids them from visiting public hospitals for minor illnesses

explanation: Frustration with long queues and drug stockouts in public hospitals drives many citizens to private clinics, cost notwithstanding. It's a clear indicator of systemic challenges!

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically confused with a benign cervical ectropion during an exam?

options.A: Uterine fibroids located in the myometrium
options.B: Benign cervical polyps protruding from the os
options.C: Early malignant tumors of the cervix
options.D: Cervicitis caused by sexually transmitted organisms

explanation: Fibroids sit deep inside the muscular wall of the uterus, way past the surface of the cervix, so they won't look like a red patch on the outer cervix. You nailed it!

question: Which of the following is NOT true about active surveillance?

options.A: It provides more accurate data than passive methods
options.B: It involves staff actively visiting sites to review records
options.C: It requires more staff time and resources
options.D: It relies entirely on waiting for clinics to mail reports

explanation: Active surveillance does not wait for reports; staff go out and look for the data. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h3)

question: How does cigarette smoking increase the risk of developing vulval tumours?

options.A: It directly increases the production of estrogen in fatty tissues
options.B: It prevents the absorption of key vitamins needed for skin health
options.C: It impairs local immunity and works with HPV to promote cell changes
options.D: It causes immediate physical trauma to the external genitalia

explanation: Correct! Smoking weakens the body's local immune response, making it harder to fight off infections like HPV that trigger bad cell changes.

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization?

options.A: To make sure syringes are sterile before an injection
options.B: To speed up the manufacturing process of new vaccines
options.C: To keep vaccines at the correct temperature until use
options.D: To freeze all vaccines solid for long-term transport

explanation: The cold chain ensures vaccines stay within safe temperature limits from the factory to the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: A patient asks how long an egg can survive and be fertilized after ovulation. What is your best response?

options.A: Up to 5 days
options.B: About 24 hours
options.C: Less than 1 hour
options.D: Exactly 1 week

explanation: Good clinical knowledge to have! An ovulated egg has a short window of about 12 to 24 hours to meet a sperm before it breaks down.

question: Which position is best for an unconscious patient who is now breathing normally and has a pulse?

options.A: High Fowler position
options.B: Prone flat on the belly
options.C: Supine with legs raised
options.D: Recovery position

explanation: Roll them into the recovery position (on their side). This keeps their airway open and safe so they don't choke if they happen to vomit.

question: In the diathesis-stress model, what does 'diathesis' refer to?

options.A: An underlying vulnerability or predisposition
options.B: The chemical name for antipsychotic drugs
options.C: A sudden environmental crisis or life event
options.D: A physical test used to measure brainwaves

explanation: Diathesis represents the biological or psychological vulnerability a person carries before a major stressor triggers an illness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h6)

question: How should you best care for a pregnant woman who has mild round ligament cramps?

options.A: Prescribing strong pain medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Telling her to ignore all pain because it is completely imaginary
options.C: Admitting her immediately to the labor ward for IV fluids
options.D: Reassuring her about normal changes and suggesting gentle stretching

explanation: Warm reassurance and simple comfort measures are all that's needed for normal pregnancy aches. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: What is the main goal of a summative evaluation at the end of an IEC campaign?

options.A: To measure the final impact and changes in community health behavior
options.B: To replace traditional rulers with modern local government staff
options.C: To check if the printing budget was spent on the exact correct date
options.D: To decide which nurse should be transferred to another clinic

explanation: Summative evaluation happens at the 'summary' or end of the project to check: did our campaign actually work? Did health habits improve? [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the main reason for putting a cold compress on a fresh insect sting?

options.A: It kills any bacteria introduced by the insect's mouthparts
options.B: It triggers immediate local histamine destruction
options.C: It completely neutralizes the chemical structure of the acid
options.D: It constricts blood vessels to slow down venom absorption

explanation: Correct! Cold causes the local blood vessels to narrow (vasoconstriction), slowing down how quickly the venom travels into the rest of the body.

question: What are the three main parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Agent, host, and environment
options.B: Source, spread, and susceptibility
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Vector, transmission, and portal

explanation: You nailed it! The epidemiological triangle consists of the infectious agent, the host who can catch it, and the environment where they meet.

question: What is male child preference?

options.A: The legal right of sons to inherit property automatically
options.B: A medical condition affecting reproductive hormone balance
options.C: A government policy encouraging larger family sizes
options.D: The cultural valuation of male offspring over female offspring

explanation: You nailed it! Male child preference simply means society values having boys more than girls due to cultural traditions.

question: What is a great lifestyle step to help restore regular ovulation in a patient with PCOS and insulin resistance?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.B: Strict bed rest for several weeks
options.C: Complete elimination of dietary water
options.D: Weight management and regular exercise

explanation: Lifestyle is powerful medicine! Getting regular exercise and managing weight helps the body handle insulin better, which naturally helps balance hormones and restore ovulation.

question: What should you do if you find a banned or unclear abbreviation on a patient's drug chart?

options.A: Cross it out and rewrite it using personal shorthand codes
options.B: Guess the intended dose based on the patient's age and weight
options.C: Administer the medication immediately to avoid treatment delays
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Safety first! Never guess when an order is unclear. Always contact the prescribing doctor or clinician to verify what they meant before giving the medication.

question: What is a semi-synthetic medication?

options.A: An animal hormone grown inside a bacterial cell
options.B: A natural substance that is chemically modified in a lab
options.C: A plant extract that has never been processed by humans
options.D: A drug made entirely from artificial laboratory chemicals

explanation: Semi-synthetic drugs start with a natural base (like a plant compound) which chemists then tweak in a lab to make it work even better.

question: A patient lies awake for hours before finally falling asleep. What do we call this?

options.A: Early morning awakening
options.B: Paradoxical insomnia
options.C: Sleep-maintenance insomnia
options.D: Sleep-onset insomnia

explanation: When someone struggles right at the beginning of the night trying to fall asleep, we call it sleep-onset insomnia ('onset' means the start!).

question: What is the primary function of sensory areas in the cerebral cortex?

options.A: To receive and interpret incoming information from the senses
options.B: To coordinate voluntary skeletal muscle movements
options.C: To generate long-term memories and emotional responses
options.D: To regulate vital involuntary functions like breathing

explanation: Sensory areas are specifically dedicated to processing raw signals arriving from the sensory organs throughout the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the sneaky trick that bacterial enzymes like beta-lactamase pull off?

options.A: They help bacteria digest human red blood cells
options.B: They destroy specific antibiotic medications
options.C: They speed up bacterial cell division
options.D: They create a thick capsule around the cell

explanation: Beta-lactamases are defense weapons for bacteria; they chop up the antibiotic before it can do its job.

question: Why is it so important to help a mother keep her bladder empty during prolonged labour?

options.A: It lowers the mother's blood pressure instantly
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing urine altogether
options.C: It stops the uterus from contracting spontaneously
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow labour

explanation: Think of the pelvic space as crowded! A full bladder gets in the way, making it harder for the baby's head to move down naturally.

question: Why do we connect our new research findings back to older, published studies?

options.A: It proves that the current researcher is smarter than past authors
options.B: It is a strict legal requirement for copyright clearance
options.C: It shows whether the new results support or challenge existing knowledge
options.D: It ensures that no new statistical tests need to be run

explanation: Well done! Connecting new data to past work helps us see the bigger picture of how nursing knowledge builds over time.

question: Which factor is consistently linked with pregnant women making better use of antenatal care?

options.A: Higher level of maternal education
options.B: Living in a densely populated urban slum
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional childbirth herbs
options.D: Having a large extended family at home

explanation: Spot on! Educated women are usually more aware of health risks, understand advice better, and feel more confident seeking professional care early.

question: What is the safest thing to do right after giving an injection with a disposable syringe?

options.A: Place the uncapped syringe on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Drop the entire syringe into a nearby sharps container
options.C: Recap the needle firmly using a two-handed technique
options.D: Break the needle off before disposal

explanation: Correct! To avoid accidental needle pricks, always drop the whole sharp device straight into a puncture-resistant container without trying to recap it.

question: What is the main purpose of secondary health prevention in clinical practice?

options.A: Detecting diseases early before symptoms appear
options.B: Preventing an illness from ever starting
options.C: Treating advanced stages of chronic disease
options.D: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke

explanation: You got it! Secondary prevention is all about catching conditions early while treatment is still super effective.

question: Why is self-care considered an absolute must for mental health nurses, rather than just a nice bonus?

options.A: Unmanaged burnout and fatigue can impair clinical judgment and compromise patient safety
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to log relaxation hours for promotion
options.C: Patients refuse care from nurses who look tired
options.D: It is the only way to avoid ever working night shifts

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Looking after your own mental health keeps your clinical judgment sharp so you can keep your patients safe.

question: Why must a patient taking the blood thinner warfarin watch how many leafy green vegetables they eat?

options.A: The food inhibits liver enzymes and causes fatal bleeding episodes
options.B: The food counteracts the blood-thinning effect, risking clot formation
options.C: The food binds to the drug in the stomach and stops absorption
options.D: The food lowers blood pressure and causes sudden fainting spells

explanation: Leafy greens are loaded with Vitamin K, which naturally helps blood clot. Since Vitamin K fights against warfarin's job, sudden changes in diet can put the patient at risk.

question: What does the term NEAT stand for in nutrition and metabolism discussions?

options.A: New Estimated Adaptation Threshold
options.B: Normal Energy Absorption Technique
options.C: Nutritional Evaluation and Assessment Tool
options.D: Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis

explanation: NEAT is all about those extra calories you burn through daily movements that aren't formal gym workouts—like walking to class, cleaning, or even fidgeting!

question: A patient with a low CD4 count has creamy white patches in their mouth that bleed easily when scraped. What is this likely to be?

options.A: Cytomegalovirus ulcers
options.B: Oral hairy leukoplakia
options.C: Oral candidiasis
options.D: Herpes simplex stomatitis

explanation: Also known as oral thrush, these removable white plaques are very common when the immune system is deeply weakened.

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement (QI) in nursing?

options.A: Cutting down nursing staff to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Punishing staff who make medication mistakes
options.C: Filing incident reports after safety errors happen
options.D: Proactively redesigning care to give patients better outcomes

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Quality improvement is all about fixing systems before errors happen, rather than just reacting after things go wrong. You've got this!

question: While looking at an ovary slide under a microscope, you spot a large fluid-filled space called an antrum. What kind of follicle is this?

options.A: Primordial follicle
options.B: Tertiary follicle
options.C: Atretic follicle
options.D: Primary follicle

explanation: You're doing great. That fluid-filled space (antrum) is the classic giveaway that you are looking at a mature or tertiary follicle.

question: A patient arrives from a terrible car crash with massive internal bleeding. What must the trauma suite have ready immediately?

options.A: Cosmetic laser equipment and soothing music
options.B: Long-term recovery beds for overnight stays
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion equipment and crash carts
options.D: Specialized eye microscopes and micro-sutures

explanation: Wonderful! Trauma suites must be stocked with rapid blood warmers and infusers to fight off hemorrhagic shock right away.

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Dehydration
options.D: Diet

explanation: In the emergency ABCDE framework, D stands for disability, which evaluates basic neurological status. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h2)

question: When washing a patient's arms or legs during a bed bath, why does the nurse stroke from the hands or feet toward the torso?

options.A: To check if the patient has broken bones in the hand
options.B: To push all dirt and sweat directly into the armpits
options.C: To make the skin stretch out and look younger
options.D: To promote venous blood return toward the heart

explanation: Brilliant! Moving your washcloth upward helps push venous blood back up toward the heart against gravity, which is great for circulation.

question: What severe complication happens when an intestinal ulcer eats all the way through the bowel wall?

options.A: Intestinal perforation
options.B: Chronic kidney failure
options.C: Pulmonary embolism
options.D: Hepatic encephalopathy

explanation: You nailed it! A break through the entire bowel wall is called a perforation—definitely a medical emergency.

question: Which eye finding is a classic sign that death has occurred?

options.A: Constricted pupils in bright light
options.B: Rapid involuntary blinking
options.C: Severe swelling of the eyelids
options.D: Fixed and dilated pupils

explanation: Well done! When the brainstem stops working, the pupils stop reacting to light and stay wide and fixed.

question: How does severe financial stress usually affect a patient managing a physical disability?

options.A: It ends their need for community support
options.B: It causes immediate bone degeneration
options.C: It makes them less likely to follow their prescribed care plan
options.D: It automatically cures their chronic condition

explanation: When money is tight, patients often have to choose between feeding their families and buying meds or attending follow-up clinics. Financial stress makes adherence very difficult!

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative research methods?

options.A: Calculating patient weights on a digital scale
options.B: Exploring human experiences and meanings in depth
options.C: Measuring precise chemical levels in the blood
options.D: Counting the exact number of pills in a bottle

explanation: That's right! Qualitative research helps us understand people's feelings, stories, and subjective experiences.

question: Why do ICUs often pause a patient's sedative medications for a short time every day?

options.A: To test the electrical activity of the heart muscles under stress
options.B: To allow family members to visit without medical equipment in the way
options.C: To ensure the patient has completely recovered from their primary disease
options.D: To reduce the duration of mechanical ventilation and prevent delirium

explanation: Giving a daily break from sedatives helps patients wake up sooner, get off the breathing machine faster, and stay mentally clear.

question: In community health nursing, who is considered the primary 'client'?

options.A: Only the children under five years old
options.B: The local government chairman
options.C: The medical director of the district hospital
options.D: The entire population of the community

explanation: Correct! While bedside nurses focus on one patient at a time, community health nurses look at the big picture and treat the whole population as their patient.

question: How should a nurse protect a patient's dignity during a bedside handover?

options.A: Speak in a very loud voice so everyone in the hallway can hear
options.B: Ask all family members to permanently leave the hospital ward
options.C: Ensure privacy curtains are drawn and sensitive details are discussed discreetly
options.D: Refuse to let the patient look at their own medical chart

explanation: Always draw privacy curtains and keep your voice soft and respectful when talking about private health matters.

question: What is an early sign of fluid overload to watch out for during rehydration therapy?

options.A: Rapid disappearance of skin pinch elasticity
options.B: Puffy eyelids and swelling around the eyes
options.C: Extreme thirst and dry cracked lips
options.D: Sunken fontanelles in infants

explanation: Puffy eyes (periorbital edema) are a classic early warning that extra fluid and sodium are starting to build up in the body's tissues.

question: A nurse asks an older patient how many times a week they eat fresh fruits and vegetables. What assessment tool is the nurse using?

options.A: Food frequency questionnaire
options.B: Direct anthropometric measurement
options.C: Biochemical marker analysis
options.D: 24-hour dietary recall

explanation: Asking how often specific foods are eaten over a weekly or monthly span is a classic food frequency questionnaire.

question: Why are young married girls at such high risk for severe anxiety and depression?

options.A: Hormonal shifts during puberty completely prevent emotional stability
options.B: Cultural traditions mandate that they remain sad for the first year
options.C: Their brains naturally produce fewer mood-regulating chemicals
options.D: They face sudden social isolation, loss of family support, and domestic pressure

explanation: Spot on. Being cut off from friends and school, then thrust into heavy adult duties without emotional readiness, causes immense psychological distress.

question: Generally speaking, what is the trade-off between joint mobility and stability?

options.A: There is no connection between mobility and stability
options.B: Greater stability usually means greater speed of movement
options.C: Mobility and stability always increase together
options.D: Greater mobility usually means lower stability

explanation: Exactly! Joints built for wide movement—like the shoulder—are easier to dislocate because they trade stability for flexibility.

question: How do mental health and mental illness connect to each other?

options.A: They are completely separate states that never overlap in a person
options.B: Mental health only applies to individuals younger than forty years
options.C: Mental illness always develops immediately after a period of stress
options.D: They exist as two opposite ends of a continuous dynamic spectrum

explanation: Think of mental health and illness as a sliding scale rather than rigid boxes. People move back and forth along this spectrum throughout their lives depending on life events and support.

question: You just finished soaking and washing your patient's hands. What is the most important thing to do before picking up the clippers?

options.A: Applying thick scented lotion to the skin
options.B: Pushing the cuticles back with force
options.C: Drying the hands and fingers thoroughly
options.D: Massaging the palms to improve circulation

explanation: Exactly! Wet hands make the clippers slippery, and trapped moisture can cause issues. Always dry them well first!

question: During the primary survey, a trauma nurse cuts away a patient's heavy jacket. What is the main reason for this action under the 'Exposure' step?

options.A: To prepare the patient for an immediate routine blood test
options.B: To comply with standard hospital laundry collection policies
options.C: To inspect the body for hidden bleeding or wounds
options.D: To make the hospital room feel cooler and more comfortable

explanation: Exposing the patient allows nurses to spot unseen injuries, though care must be taken to prevent heat loss. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to cure viral infections like the common cold?

options.A: Antibiotics are destroyed by stomach acid before reaching viral cells
options.B: Viruses mutate too quickly for white blood cells to recognize them
options.C: Viruses hide inside healthy red blood cells away from medicines
options.D: Viruses do not possess the cellular structures that antibiotics target

explanation: Remember, antibiotics attack bacterial walls or parts that viruses simply don't have. That's why taking antibiotics for a viral flu won't help!

question: Why is a vague phrase like 'improving community health' not ideal as a project indicator?

options.A: It can only be evaluated by international health organizations
options.B: It lacks specific targets and measurable parameters to track progress accurately
options.C: It is too expensive to write down in official government records
options.D: It focuses only on financial expenditures instead of patient care

explanation: If a goal doesn't have clear numbers and timeframes, it's impossible to prove whether things actually got better!

question: What is one of the biggest goals of home-based nursing care?

options.A: Reducing the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: Ensuring the patient moves permanently to a nursing home
options.C: Preventing unnecessary hospital readmissions
options.D: Eliminating the involvement of family members

explanation: Exactly! By managing health well at home, we keep patients comfortable and out of crowded hospital beds.

question: What kind of pupil change do you expect to see in a patient with organophosphate poisoning (cholinergic toxidrome)?

options.A: Pinpoint pupils
options.B: Unreactive fixed pupils
options.C: Widely dilated pupils
options.D: Unequal pupil sizes

explanation: Organophosphates overstimulate the nervous system, which famously causes the pupils to shrink down to tiny, pinpoint sizes (miosis).

question: How should a school set up a new nursing simulation lab to best help students?

options.A: Keep all medical tools locked away in another building
options.B: Make it look and feel just like a real hospital ward
options.C: Put in rows of normal desks facing a chalkboard
options.D: Take out all hospital beds to leave open floor space

explanation: Realistic simulation labs help you get comfortable with hospital layouts and tools before you step onto the actual ward.

question: Which clinical encounter offers nurses a key opportunity to identify victims of early marriage?

options.A: Annual hospital administration meetings
options.B: Surgical safety checklist briefings
options.C: Routine occupational health screenings
options.D: Antenatal and maternity clinic visits

explanation: Young pregnant girls frequently interact with maternity nurses, making prenatal clinics ideal settings for identifying underage and coerced unions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h5)

question: What patient position is standard and most appropriate for inserting a rectal suppository?

options.A: Upright sitting position in a chair
options.B: Prone position lying flat on the stomach
options.C: Sims position on the left side
options.D: Flat on the back with legs held high

explanation: The Sims position naturally aligns with the downward curve of the sigmoid colon and rectum, making insertion easier. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h7)

question: What is the most important nursing priority for a patient taking long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART)?

options.A: Ensuring the patient sleeps on a firm mattress
options.B: Encouraging strict adherence to the medication schedule
options.C: Restricting all water intake to prevent fluid overload
options.D: Massaging the arms daily to improve circulation

explanation: You got it! Sticking strictly to medication times keeps the virus suppressed and stops drug-resistant strains from popping up.

question: Why can relying too much on assistive technology become a problem in patient care?

options.A: It can reduce human interaction and lead to patient isolation
options.B: It automatically cures all chronic illnesses within days
options.C: It forces patients to perform rigorous physical exercises
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical research

explanation: You're doing great! While tech is helpful, leaning on machines too much can cut down on the warm, meaningful human contact patients need.

question: A community nurse partners with local farmers and school headmasters to combat child malnutrition. Which concept does this action best demonstrate?

options.A: Private health insurance
options.B: Intersectoral linkages
options.C: Tertiary medical isolation
options.D: Acute hospital management

explanation: Partnering with agriculture and education sectors to address malnutrition is a classic example of intersectoral linkages. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: Why is it so important to set clear, specific objectives during the planning stage?

options.A: It guides what activities to do and helps measure future success
options.B: It replaces the need to collect baseline data
options.C: It guarantees that no unexpected problems will ever occur
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to work in rural areas

explanation: Clear objectives act like a map. They show you your daily steps and let you check later whether you actually reached your destination.

question: How were patients typically treated inside early asylums?

options.A: Trained in useful vocational skills
options.B: Involved in daily group therapy sessions
options.C: Given regular rest periods and nutritious meals
options.D: Chained, neglected, and viewed as public spectacles

explanation: Conditions were brutal, and facilities even charged admission fees for tourists to come and stare at the inmates. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h2)

question: How should a nurse safely feed a baby admitted with active neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Administering intravenous nutrition exclusively for weeks
options.B: Encouraging frequent and forceful oral suckling
options.C: Using a nasogastric or orogastric tube
options.D: Using an open cup held against the lower lip

explanation: You got it! Trying to feed by mouth can trigger dangerous jaw spasms and choke the baby, making tube feeding the safest choice.

question: What legal charge might you face if you force medication on a clear-headed adult patient who says no?

options.A: Defamation
options.B: Battery
options.C: Invasion of privacy
options.D: Breach of contract

explanation: Exactly! Giving unwanted treatment to a competent adult who refused it counts as battery under the law. Always respect patient autonomy!

question: In holistic palliative care, who is considered the 'unit of care'?

options.A: The patient and their family combined
options.B: Only the patient experiencing the symptoms
options.C: The attending physician and senior nurse
options.D: The immediate hospital nursing ward team

explanation: Think of it this way: an illness affects everyone in the household, so we care for both the patient and their loved ones as a team.

question: Why do nurses need to review and update diet plans from time to time?

options.A: Because patients get bored eating the same foods for more than three days
options.B: Because hospital regulations require rewriting charts weekly
options.C: Because food items change their vitamin content every single month
options.D: Because client needs, health status, and life circumstances change over time

explanation: Life isn't static, and neither is health! Regular checks ensure the diet plan keeps up with the patient's changing body and life.

question: How does the lower esophageal sphincter help protect you from GERD (heartburn)?

options.A: It acts like a muscular valve that stops stomach acid from flowing upward
options.B: It neutralizes food before it drops into the stomach
options.C: It secretes thick mucus to coat the top of the stomach
options.D: It controls how fast food leaves the stomach for the small intestine

explanation: The lower esophageal sphincter is your body's one-way valve. It stays tightly closed and only opens to let food travel down into the stomach.

question: What do second-order neurons typically do in ascending sensory pathways?

options.A: They secrete neurotransmitters onto sweat glands
options.B: They directly connect skin receptors to motor neurons
options.C: They cross the midline and ascend to the thalamus
options.D: They store long-term sensory memories in the frontal lobe

explanation: You got it! Second-order neurons cross over (decussate) to the opposite side of the spinal cord or brainstem before heading up to the thalamus.

question: Because of where the breathing centers are located in the brain, which vital sign must a nurse monitor most closely in pontine injuries?

options.A: Orthostatic blood pressure changes
options.B: Core body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Peripheral oxygen saturation trends
options.D: Respiratory rate and breathing pattern

explanation: Spot on! Since the pons helps control breathing rhythms, keeping a close eye on your patient's respiratory pattern can save their life.

question: Which group of people should be involved during a community health situation analysis?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting local tourist attractions
options.B: International pharmaceutical company sales representatives
options.C: Local stakeholders like traditional leaders and women's groups
options.D: Only doctors from the federal capital city

explanation: True community health relies on involving local leaders and residents who understand their environment and hold social influence. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why must a nurse demonstrate the call bell system immediately upon a patient's arrival?

options.A: It distracts the patient from their current physical pain
options.B: It gives the patient a direct way to call for help when needed
options.C: It proves to the visiting family members that the equipment works
options.D: Hospital policy requires it to be tested every single hour

explanation: Showing the patient the call bell ensures they can easily summon assistance for urgent needs like using the toilet or managing sudden pain. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main reason we give packed red blood cells to a patient?

options.A: To replace lost clotting factors
options.B: To boost white blood cell counts
options.C: To improve oxygen-carrying capacity
options.D: To correct low serum albumin levels

explanation: You've got this! Packed red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, which acts like little transport buses carrying oxygen from the lungs to every corner of the body.

question: Which of these is a common misconception about publishing a research paper?

options.A: It requires writing down the methods and study results
options.B: It takes time and careful adherence to journal guidelines
options.C: It helps hospital administrators make policy decisions
options.D: It automatically changes clinical behavior at the bedside

explanation: That's a tricky one, but you've got it! Just publishing a paper doesn't automatically change clinical practice; nurses still need active encouragement and training to apply it.

question: Where do the bones of your skull and jaw mostly come from during early development?

options.A: Visceral endoderm
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Pelvic mesoderm
options.D: Cardiac jelly

explanation: Think of neural crest cells as great travelers—they migrate forward into the head region early on to form your face and skull bones!

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative pressure isolation room?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Droplet precautions
options.D: Standard precautions

explanation: Negative pressure rooms prevent tiny airborne germs from drifting out into the hallway when the door is opened. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team needed for comprehensive FGM care?

options.A: Patients refuse to speak to nurses unless a doctor is present
options.B: Surgeons are legally required to manage all aspects of nursing care
options.C: Medical insurance only covers care if multiple specialists sign off
options.D: The physical, psychological, and obstetric needs of survivors are complex

explanation: Because FGM affects physical health, childbirth, and mental health all at once, teamwork among different specialists gives the patient the best care possible. You're doing awesome!

question: Which of the following is classified as a barrier method of contraception?

options.A: Male and female condoms
options.B: Copper intrauterine device
options.C: Progestin-only injectable
options.D: Basal body temperature tracking

explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent sperm from entering the female reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h3)

question: Which deficiency disease is caused by a serious lack of Vitamin C?

options.A: Beriberi
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Scurvy
options.D: Pellagra

explanation: You got it! Without enough Vitamin C, your body can't make collagen properly, leading to scurvy (bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds).

question: A nurse finishes cleaning and dressing severe chest burns on a young girl rescued from breast ironing. What is the next essential step in her holistic care?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with basic oral antibiotics
options.B: Involving child protection and mental health services
options.C: Telling the mother to return only if new blisters appear
options.D: Scheduling a follow-up appointment in six months

explanation: Ensuring the child's immediate physical and emotional safety through protection agencies and counseling is a top priority. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is the main job of a Rapid Response Center during an emergency?

options.A: To conduct routine annual physical examinations for community residents
options.B: To serve as a permanent long-term housing facility for displaced families
options.C: To manufacture emergency medical supplies and pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.D: To coordinate swift interventions and manage resource distribution during crises

explanation: Think of a Rapid Response Center as the command post. When a crisis hits, it organizes the rescue efforts and gets supplies where they're needed fast!

question: Why must observations be independent when doing a Chi-Square test?

options.A: To eliminate the need for calculating expected frequencies
options.B: To guarantee that all data points are continuous numbers
options.C: To ensure the sample size is always larger than one thousand
options.D: To prevent the same patient from being counted in multiple cells

explanation: Exactly! Independent observations mean each patient is only counted once, keeping our groups separate and our results accurate.

question: How is 'prevalence' different from 'incidence'?

options.A: Prevalence only counts patients who are currently hospitalized
options.B: Prevalence includes all existing cases, both old and new
options.C: Prevalence is only used for vaccine trial evaluations
options.D: Prevalence measures how fast a disease spreads in a week

explanation: While incidence is just the *new* cases, prevalence is the grand total of everyone currently living with the condition (old and new together). Easy peasy!

question: A patient suddenly loses their job and becomes homeless. Which category of health determinants is mainly at play here?

options.A: Biological determinants
options.B: Social and environmental determinants
options.C: Genetic determinants
options.D: Neurochemical determinants

explanation: You got it! Things like a stable job, housing, and financial security belong to our social and environmental surroundings, which heavily influence our peace of mind.

question: Why do nurses take out the inner cannula to clean or replace it?

options.A: To deflate the cuff automatically
options.B: To prevent dried secretions from blocking the airway
options.C: To change the size of the outer tube
options.D: To allow the patient to drink water safely

explanation: Mucus loves to build up inside the tube! Cleaning or swapping the inner cannula keeps the airway clear so the patient can breathe easily.

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements to women in early pregnancy?

options.A: To accelerate infant tooth eruption
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy helps protect the baby's developing brain and spinal cord. Super important vitamin!

question: What is the best position for a patient receiving a flatus tube?

options.A: High Fowler's sitting position
options.B: Left lateral Sims' position
options.C: Prone position flat on the stomach
options.D: Supine position with legs flat

question: A pregnant woman at 38 weeks gestation has a single baby lying head-down and normal blood pressure. Is she a candidate for home delivery?

options.A: Only if she refuses to take routine blood tests

options.D: No, all women must deliver in a tertiary hospital
